title: Graph basics
learn: vertices/edges, directed/undirected, weighted, adjacency list vs matrix, degree, building a graph from edges
hook: Graphs model maps, networks, dependencies and social connections, and they're a big part of medium/hard interviews. It all starts with one habit: turn the edge list into an adjacency list.

explain.prompt: Explain the ways to represent a graph, and when you'd pick an adjacency list over an adjacency matrix.
keyPoints: a graph is nodes plus edges; edges can be directed or undirected, weighted or not
adjacency list: node → neighbours, O(V + E) space, neighbours listed in O(degree)
adjacency matrix: O(V²) space, O(1) edge check; only worth it for dense graphs
undirected edges are stored in both directions; in-degree/out-degree count arrows in and out
